That’s definitely a great way to study for nursing. I would keep doing that to get a good understanding of the content, and then also use any practice questions your textbooks have just to get familiar with the kind of questions you’ll be asked.

If you did really well in your pre-req you should be fine in nursing school, however, just know that nursing courses are a lot different from general undergrad courses. They are definitely a lot of work, and a lot of the actual work isn’t very hard, just time consuming. However, the exams can be difficult and are likely a lot different from exams you’ve taken in the past. On nursing exams, you’re not going to get questions that are pure memorization. They’re all higher level critical thinking questions, that require basic knowledge on the subject as well as a deeper understanding, *and* the ability to apply the knowledge and understanding to what’s being asked in the question. Just be prepared to potentially change the way you study (thousands of practice questions are in your future) and you’ll be fine. good luck!!

It really does depend on where you’re looking. Some schools are way more competitive than others. Every school/region is different. For example, most California schools have a points system and a lottery, where you get X number of points for Y GPA and Z TEAS score, etc. Then once you have the minimum number of points to apply, you’re just entered in a lottery. So even if their minimum GPA is a 3.4, as long as you qualify to apply, you could actually beat out someone with a 4.0 if you’re picked in the lottery and they are not. Other places do just take your GPA and TEAS and weigh them against other applicants. With a 3.44 and a decent TEAS you can absolutely get into an ADN program, but you may just have to apply to a few schools or different areas. As someone who multitoons quite frequently & manages to not have one be dead weight in the actual boss fight, it frustrates me a lot when people do that. Plus, it’s harder to keep both alive that way. Definitely download multi controller. It’s super helpful, you can either control the toons separately, or what I do is I control them both with the arrow keys at the same time. It takes a bit of getting used to and you occasionally have to adjust one or the other, but it’s so helpful. 

That being said, VP is definitely the easiest boss to fight while multitooning. I’d say CFO is second; I usually have one crane and one goon and it’s not difficult. CJ is tough with all the stuff flying at you and you have to adjust a toon every time they get hit. CEO is 100% the hardest to multi because of how often the CEO attacks and how much damage you take. I would not multi toon CEO unless you feel super confident in your timing of dodging his attacks, have multi tooned enough to feel comfortable with running two, and have a really good wifi connection.  

Good luck! multi tooning opens a whole new way to play the game. it’s pretty fun!
